doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lee Morgan and his early death
summary: Young says Lee Morgan was on his way to greatness when a woman shot him at Slug's.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: How about some of the other trumpet players that come up in the ‗50s like Lee Morgan?
Well, Lee Morgan didn‘t live long. Lee was good, he would have been here. He would have, people don‘t know how good Lee was going to be. See he died before he got… what did happen to him?
That‘s right, something happened to him, about a woman.

He was on his way, man, but he got wasted. He was on his way. He wouldn‘t have, I don‘t think he would have blown anybody out, but he‘d be right up there with all the cats like Roy and some of them guys… in that bracket, in other words, is what I‘m trying to say he would have been if he lived, because he was well on his way, he was very young man when he got wasted. He got killed. That woman killed him. I forget how that happened.
It was either his wife or a jealous girlfriend one of the two. I think his wife might have found he was…
It was his wife or it was some woman. It was something like that.
And shot him. I think it was at Slug‘s.
Right in the, on the band stand! [laughs]
